timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Ever pondered the mysteries of the moon?
Well, scientists have recently unveiled a lunar enigma.
A reaction took place deep within our celestial neighbour about 3.5 billion years ago.
Iron in magma exchanged with magnesium in adjacent rocks,
altering the magma's chemical and physical properties.
A unique rock type called high-type azults.
These rocks, intriguing researchers for years, now have their origins explained.
Thanks to meticulous lab experiments and spectroscopic examinations of moon rocks,
scientists discovered a distinct isotopic composition.
The interaction between melt and solids within lunar magma is the birthplace of these rocks.
A puzzle in lunar geology solved, unraveling the moon's geological past one rock at a time.
